$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-REHAB-005 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §10.8 and the RF-REHAB-005 inventory entry. Architecture-source rule: evidence_claim_ids intentionally empty per v1.2 §4.3. Expresses schedule and total-load reconciliation STRUCTURE only: strength, eccentric exposure, running, sprinting, kicking, matches, conditioning, and concurrent-injury work must be composed into one weekly load plan; avoid duplicate tissue stress and unaccounted stacking; if the schedule cannot satisfy all active constraints, modify, restrict, or block the plan. Unknown external load stays unknown and triggers governed missing-data behavior, never silent clearance. No dosage, exercise selection, complete plan, RTT, or RTS logic; schedule fit alone is not progression or readiness; safety precedence preserved; does not bypass RF-REHAB-001/002/003/004 or override RF-SAF-006/RF-DX-008/RF-SEV-004/RF-SEV-005. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.

input_contract.$comment: The load domains taken verbatim from v1.2 §10.8, plus the external-load inputs that must be considered. Unknown external load remains unknown and triggers governed missing-data behaviour, never silent clearance.

decision_contract.$comment: Schedule and total-load reconciliation structure only. All active load domains compose into one weekly load plan; duplicate tissue stress and unaccounted stacking are avoided; schedule conflicts trigger modify/restrict/block. No dosage, exercise selection, complete plan, RTT, or RTS; schedule fit alone is not progression or readiness. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Architecture normative source; MUST; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. Architecture refs preserved per source: V3.1-11 (concurrent & secondary injuries) and V3.1-13.3 (scheduling & load coordination). No evidence_claim_ids are cited (legitimately empty per v1.2 §4.3 — architecture rules need not invent evidence claims; [] means 'none required', not 'missing'). Per §10.8 logic preserved exactly: strength, eccentric exposure, running, sprinting, kicking, matches, conditioning, and concurrent-injury work must be composed into one weekly load plan. Per §10.8 decision preserved exactly: avoid duplicate tissue stress and unaccounted stacking; if the schedule cannot satisfy all active constraints, modify, restrict, or block the plan. External training, competition, match, kicking, high-speed running, heavy strength, eccentric overload, and other-injury-rehab loads are considered and never silently assumed zero/absent; unknown external load remains unknown and triggers governed missing-data behaviour rather than silent clearance. Schedule fit alone is not progression and schedule compatibility alone is not readiness. Safety-state choice (read §10.8 exactly): §10.8 does NOT assign a closed V3.1 safety state — it describes total-load reconciliation and a modify/restrict/block conflict response — so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty, and the schedule-conflict behaviour is represented in decision_contract; no safety state was inferred by analogy (terminal REHAB_BLOCKED for an irreconcilable concurrent-injury conflict is owned by RF-REHAB-006 / RF-SAF-006). The rule creates no dosage, selects no exercises or complete exercise plan, generates no complete rehab plan, and produces no return-to-training or return-to-sport decision; it does not bypass RF-REHAB-001/002/003/004 and does not override RF-SAF-006, RF-DX-008, RF-SEV-004, or RF-SEV-005; uncertainty is preserved when schedule, external-load, match-load, training-load, concurrent-injury, or monitoring data are incomplete. Rehabilitation scheduling/total-load rule, not a safety rule. No scheduling engine is authored here (deferred to the later rehab selection and planning objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
